question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed opt-in `gateway.readiness` contract, including `{}` activation semantics, fail-closed required `Unknown` conditions, and an activation-scoped plugin readiness-provider API?
rationale: The PR defines new configuration and plugin API surface with deliberate upgrade behavior; source review cannot determine whether these are the product boundaries maintainers want to support permanently.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow readiness v1
options.body: Accept the opt-in core contract while preserving legacy readiness by default, then require an implementation issue and explicit compatibility tests before runtime rollout.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Request that the RFC defer plugin-provider registration or `{}` activation semantics until the core readiness result and operator selection model are proven.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Keep the RFC draft until maintainers have capacity to own the public readiness and plugin compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow readiness v1
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in core contract while preserving legacy readiness by default, then require an implementation issue and explicit compatibility tests before runtime rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate for clarifying the coordinated proposal and linked implementation stack, while acceptance itself still requires a repository maintainer decision.
